name: Palak Paneer
steps: Wash the spinach thoroughly in several changes of water, removing grit and tough stems. Finely chop the tomato and cut the paneer into even bite-size cubes.
Blanch the spinach in a pot of boiling water for 1–2 minutes, just until wilted. Drain, cool with cold water, drain again and blend to a puree; reserve the measured recipe water for the sauce.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and let the cumin sizzle until fragrant. Add the tomato and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until soft and pulpy with no firm pieces.
Add the spinach puree and measured water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for about 4 minutes, stirring the base; use a lower heat if the thick sauce spits.
Add paneer and salt, folding gently so the cubes stay intact. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until the paneer is heated through; prolonged hard boiling can make it rubbery.
Turn off the heat and stir in cream. The sauce should coat the paneer but still be spoonable; loosen with a little hot water if needed, then serve.
tips: Keep paneer at a gentle simmer to avoid a rubbery texture.
substitutions: For a cream finish, plain whisked curd may work: cool the pan and add gradually. Recheck dietary filters before substituting.
